quotes.text: Save payment details during a payment in your mobile app.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: The mobile Payment Element only supports `setup_future_usage` with cards and US bank accounts.
For these payment methods, the final payment status isn’t known when the `PaymentSheet` completes, and instead succeeds or fails later.
Collect explicit consent from the customer for this specific use.

findings: The canonical 2026-11-07 capture says the purpose is to save payment details during a mobile payment and routes to three platform-specific Payment Sheet URLs (new raw 1–15). It does not capture any of those variant bodies. The matched detailed capture was fetched 2026-04-22 despite its filename and identifies its historical URL variants as mobile-ui=payment-element (old raw 1–12, 1056–1060, 1926–1930). The diff’s final removed paragraph and first added URL share physical line 2919; both exact raw endings distinguish them (old raw 2917–2918, new raw 13–15).

The summary’s central API pattern is historical. The April guide separates a server-created PaymentIntent, a customer-configured Accounts v2 Account or Customers v1 Customer, and a temporary, scoped CustomerSession, matching `customer_account` or `customer` to the identity across server examples. It shows the mobile component and initial `setup_future_usage` setting separately from a later off-session confirmation attempt (old raw 115–130, 140–231, 634–724; source lines 13–44, 63–78).

The existing summary needs baseline corrections unrelated to the navigation change. It omits purpose-specific consent and the redisplay distinction, has no warning that the archived client samples and endpoint disagree for React Native or that Android’s optional FlowController uses a different credential example, and states an unsupported completion-on-selection and success-only delayed outcome (source lines 13–85; old raw 22–33, 549–552, 620–644, 1567–1582, 1846–1867, 2070–2152, 2248–2355, 2381–2413, 2486–2504).
historical_claims_to_preserve: The 2026-04-22 guide described saving during an initial PaymentIntent purchase, with a distinct Terminal card-present flow, explicit agreement for the intended use, record retention, and an `allow_redisplay` boundary for future display (old raw 8–33, 634–641).

The 2026-04-22 guide used the `mobile_payment_element` CustomerSession component and initial `setup_future_usage`, with the cards and US bank accounts limit scoped to that setting. It shows customer-configured Accounts v2 with `customer_account` or Customers v1 with `customer`; the dated Accounts v2 text says generally available for Connect and public preview for others, requiring a preview API version for participants (old raw 115–183, 187–231, 642–648).

The 2026-04-22 guide described a new server-side PaymentIntent for a later off-session payment attempt using the same customer identity and saved PaymentMethod ID, with amount, currency, `off_session: true` and `confirm: true`. An unmet authentication exemption can produce an error (old raw 640–724).

The 2026-04-22 guide separates completing client collection, processing, succeeding, and failing. Delayed payments can still be pending when the sheet completes and later succeed or fail. Server events establish payment status (old raw 549–552, 620–632, 1567–1581, 2411–2413, 2486–2498).
conflicts: The old React Native endpoint returns `customerSessionClientSecret`, but both identity branches of its client example instead expect `ephemeralKey` and pass `customerEphemeralKeySecret`; its optional custom flow also uses an ephemeral-key example (old raw 2098–2103, 2144–2149, 2248–2355, 2884–2897). Android’s ordinary Sheet uses `createWithCustomerSession`, while its optional FlowController passes `ephemeralKeySecret` (old raw 1368–1396, 1846–1867). Keep the dated sample differences visible and avoid treating the credentials as interchangeable. Source lines 13–58 otherwise imply a uniform setup.

The source lines 80–85 say the Sheet returns `.completed` immediately on selecting a delayed method and describe only eventual success. The old captures of the integration distinguish selection, completing the sheet, and later success or failure; the `processing` row separately describes a pending state and an optional digital-goods decision (old raw 549–552, 620–632, 1868–1924, 2411–2413, 2486–2498). The archived text does not make earlier fulfillment a signal of payment success.

The in-app concept lines 58–67 can conflate a broader saved-method matrix with the narrower historical `setup_future_usage` limit and says automatic consent handles global compliance. The old guide explicitly assigns responsibility for the intended future use to the merchant and requires purpose-specific consent (old raw 22–33, 115–130, 634–638). A reciprocal source route should warn about both distinctions. The saved-method concept’s mobile route at line 154 should be date-scoped and preserve the distinction from its web `payment_element` example at lines 46–67.
unresolved_questions: The pinned 2026-11-07 capture does not establish the content or behavior of its linked platform variants, current SDK/API compatibility, or whether Stripe later reconciled the archived CustomerSession and ephemeral-key examples.

The older capture's label `mobile-ui=payment-element` and newer link label `mobile-ui=payment-sheet` identify different captured routes. The pinned materials do not establish whether this reflects a current product or API migration.

findings: Preserve the 2026-04-22 detailed raw and add the 2026-11-07 capture as a dated variant index. Scope the historical cards/US-bank restriction to mobile `setup_future_usage` and keep saving during an initial PaymentIntent distinct from accepting delayed methods or using a SetupIntent (source lines 6–17 and 80–95; old raw 115–132, 549–552; new raw 5–15).

Restore the two server identity alternatives and purpose-specific consent. Qualify later off-session charging as an attempt with amount and currency and possible authentication failure; the abbreviated snippet omits both required transaction inputs from the documented pattern (source lines 19–44 and 63–78; old raw 115–130, 634–724).

Retain dated iOS example and return-URL scope. Route Android and React Native credential discrepancies explicitly. Restore the server event/state boundary and the possibility of processing or failure (source lines 47–85; old raw 330–379, 549–555, 620–632, 1368–1396, 1846–1867, 2070–2152, 2248–2355, 2411–2424, 2486–2498).
conflicts: Source lines 80–85 say `.completed` occurs immediately on method selection and give only a success outcome, whereas old raw 549–552, 620–632, 1868–1924 and 2486–2498 separate sheet completion from a pending or terminal outcome.

Source lines 13–44 imply a common CustomerSession client path, while old raw 1846–1867 and 2248–2355 contain client examples with an ephemeral-key secret. React Native’s server examples return the CustomerSession secret (old raw 2098–2103 and 2144–2149).

Source lines 89–90 link to both concepts, but the in-app concept Sources lines 90–116 lack a reciprocal route and its line 67 conflicts with old raw 22–33 and 634–638 regarding merchant responsibility for consent and redisplay. The saved-method concept’s mobile source route at line 154 omits the capture date and UI boundary.
source_assessments.reason: The raw delta supplies navigation only. The current summary makes materially misleading historical implementation and delayed-outcome claims and omits the consent boundary. Correct those separately while routing both dated raw captures and retaining the historical evidence.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/save-during-payment, the 2026-11-07 snapshot establishes the purpose of saving payment details during an in-app payment and links to iOS, Android, and React Native Payment Sheet variants. New raw lines 5-15 contain the index and no platform body, so prerequisites, API identities, client setup, and outcomes come from the detailed 2026-04-22 capture. Old raw lines 109-132 and 140-231 show a server-created PaymentIntent with `setup_future_usage` limited to cards and US bank accounts in the captured mobile flow, a customer-configured Accounts v2 Account (`customer_account`) or Customers v1 Customer (`customer`), and a separate scoped CustomerSession whose client secret is returned to the app along with the PaymentIntent client secret, identity and publishable key. Old raw lines 549-552 and 620-632 distinguish Sheet completion, processing, payment success, and failure. Old raw lines 634-724 require consent for redisplay and describe a separate off-session PaymentIntent attempt that can encounter authentication failure. source-stripe-inapp-save-during-payment.md retains the core historical pattern, but needs the missing consent and identity qualifications, the inconsistent React Native and Android credential examples, and a correction to the delayed-state description.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/save-during-payment, new raw lines 5-15 replace the detailed canonical response with navigation to `mobile-ui=payment-sheet` variants. Old raw lines 8-12, 1056-1060 and 1926-1930 label the historical detailed variants `mobile-ui=payment-element`. This is a capture-scope change, with no demonstrated substantive product or API change. Keep the 2026-04-22 capture as dated authority for merchant consent and written agreement, mobile `setup_future_usage` method limits, Account versus Customer identity, scoped server credentials, preview version for Accounts v2 preview participants, and `allow_redisplay` (old raw lines 22-33, 115-130 and 634-648). Keep the Android FlowController and React Native ephemeral-key examples distinct from the CustomerSession server payload (old raw lines 1846-1867, 2098-2103, 2144-2149 and 2248-2355). In source-stripe-inapp-save-during-payment.md and related concept routes, correct completion-on-selection, make delayed success or failure depend on server-observed payment status, qualify the cards/US-bank limit to this save setting, and preserve the merchant’s consent responsibility. A client completion, return URL, saved method, or initial setup cannot establish final payment success, settlement, or future off-session success (old raw lines 549-555, 620-632 and 676-681).
